sources.read: Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: owners of units subject to Chapter 37 must report; non-owner-occupied units require owner/manager contact, business registration number if any, square footage, bedrooms/bathrooms, vacancy/occupancy dates, base rent in $250 increments and utilities; reporting due March 1 annually for buildings with fewer than 10 units (operative March 1, 2023); license under Sections 37.3(a)(1)-(2) after substantial compliance; suspension during noncompliance, prospective restoration, tenant does not owe increase for suspension months.

Chunk 0 of 5. Confirms: annual increase = 60% of CPI, capped at 7%; banking under 37.3(a)(2) subject to Section 37.15; capital-improvement 10% rule; notice and additional-occupant provisions in later chunks as cited in canonical edition. Only chunk 0 re-read this session; later-chunk propositions are not re-asserted here beyond what chunk 0 shows.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: all owners must report via Rent Board Portal; tenant-occupied units receive a rent increase license after submission; license automatically generated for non-owner-occupied units; must have current license before any annual/banked increase can go into effect; license need not be included with notice; reporting free; deadline March 1, late submission allowed but notice unenforceable without license on effective date; no monetary penalties for late filing; information submitted is public.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: Nov 9, 2026 notice re File #261020 (not enacted, subject to change; would apply to banked notices on/after Sept 15, 2026); banking requires 24 full months without any increase or the skipped amount is lost; banked amounts do not expire, do not compound or prorate, add percentages then multiply by current base rent; notice must state dollar amount, percentage, effective date, and banked portion; 30-day notice, 90-day if >10%, +5 days if mailed; use percentage in effect on effective date.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: 1.6% effective March 1, 2026 through Feb 28, 2027; license required before imposing annual/banked increases; calculate on base rent only (includes housing services, excludes temporary passthroughs/fluctuating charges); cannot round up; first increase 12 months after lease began; anniversary-date rules; 30/90-day notice +5 mail; additional-occupant charge prohibited even if lease provides for it.

Full PDF (1 chunk). Confirms: 1.6% for 3/1/26-2/28/27; 1.4% for 3/1/25-2/28/26; 1.7% for 3/1/24-2/28/25; 3.6% for 3/1/23-2/29/24; 2.3% for 3/1/22-2/28/23; 0.7% for 3/1/21-2/28/22; 1.8% for 3/1/20-2/28/21; full table back to 1982 matches hub/data.json rates for every period checked.

sources.publisher: SF Rent Board Rules Part IV (sf.gov)
sources.read: Chunks 0, 1, 3 of 4. Confirms Rule 4.10(a): notice must state which portion is annual/banked, capital-improvement, utility passthrough, RAP loan; Rule 4.12(a): banked amount may only be given at time of annual increase, 12 months must elapse, no compounding, no rounding up; Rule 4.12(b): landlord must inform tenant which portion is banked and the dates it is based on (failure to include does not render increase null and void).

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms Civil Code 827(b): written notice by personal delivery or mail under CCP 1013; 30 days if increase is 10% or less (alone or combined in prior 12 months), 90 days if greater than 10%.

Chunk 0 of 3. Confirms AB 1482 cap: 5% + CPI or 10%, whichever lower; subdivision (d)(3) exempts housing subject to local rent control restricting increases to less than subdivision (a). Later chunks not re-read this session.
Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: AB 1482 maximum 8.8% in SF for Aug 1, 2026-July 31, 2027 (5% + 3.8% CPI); does NOT apply to units under SF Rent Ordinance increase limitations; local protections remain.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms Costa-Hawkins Civil Code 1954.53(a) initial-rent and (d) occupant-change framework as summarized on SF.gov S27/S29. Full subdivision (d) text not re-read this session; this session relies on S27/S29 summaries for (d).

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: 180-day retaliation bar under stated conditions (tenant not in default, protected activity); subdivision (f) preserves lawful cause; subdivision (d) separate retaliation for organizing/association activity with tenant burden of producing evidence. Not an automatic moratorium on every increase.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms FEHA 12955(a): unlawful to discriminate/harass because of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, genetic information; (f) retaliation for opposing unlawful practices.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms federal Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability. No general federal percentage cap for private unsubsidized housing is stated on this page; none is asserted in this session's summary.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms 37.10B(a) bad-faith harassment list including (a)(5) rent increase imposed with intent to defraud/intimidate/coerce into vacating in circumvention of eviction protections, and (a)(9) discrimination violations.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: unlawful to sell or use an algorithmic device (revenue-management software using nonpublic competitor data to advise on rent/occupancy); aggregated public-data reports that do not recommend rents are excluded; penalties up to $1,000 per violation.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: $59.00 per dwelling unit for 2026-27; deadline March 1; exemption request deadline Dec 14, 2026 for 2027 fee; 50% recovery ($29.50) only if paid in full and tenant in occupancy Nov 1, penalties not recoverable; fee exemption does not satisfy Housing Inventory reporting.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: units built on/before June 13, 1979 may have rent control + eviction protection; check Property Information Map; counselor 415-252-4600. Official parcel coverage for the reported building was not reviewed this session and stays blank/flagged.

Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms: Rent Board cannot refer to individual attorneys; no lawyer needed to file a Rent Board petition; tenant resources include Open Door Legal Sunset Office (1722 Irving St, 94122) and Housing Rights Committee; listing does not guarantee free representation for notice review.

Chunks 0, 4, 6 of 10 retrieved. Confirms official guide identity (Rev. 02/01/22). Rent-increase/fixed-term pages not located in chunks read this session; this session does not quote S20 for any proposition and relies on SF.gov + Civil Code for timing/lease points.
Chunk 0 of 2. Confirms CCP 1013(a): mail service complete at deposit; 5-calendar-day extension if mailing and address both in California.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms Nov 24, 2025 announcement: proposed settlement, allegations about nonpublic competitor information, not a final adjudication and not evidence of typical conduct by every corporate landlord.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: tenant may petition to defer annual increase for failure to repair/maintain; petition due no later than 60 days after tenant receives notice; anniversary date unaffected by deferral.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms verbatim: rental income from one residential structure consisting of fewer than four units is not, by reason of that fact alone, required to obtain a business registration certificate; other business activity, payroll expense, or short-term rental income can trigger registration.
Chunk 0 of 5. Confirms general registration rule and the same fewer-than-four-units carve-out; registration is a general business-tax registration, not a rent-increase license.

Full page (1 chunk) on 2026-11-11. Confirms: File #261020, Status Pending Committee Action, Introduced 9/15/2026, no final action, no enactment date. Not law. Title: cap banked + capital-improvement increases at 10% per year for next three years.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: 6.14 unlimited increase when last original occupant vacates if timely 6.14 notice served (generally 60 days reasonable), on co-tenant or subtenant; Costa-Hawkins unlimited increase on lawful subtenant/assignee who did not reside before Jan 1, 1996, co-tenant excluded; no petition required but determination petition available.

sources.read: Chunk 0 of 11. Confirms Part VI covers petition-based justifications (operating/maintenance, capital improvements, comparables, etc.) requiring Rent Board approval. Section 6.14 text in later chunks not re-read this session; relied on via S27/S29.

Full page (1 chunk). Confirms: landlord not required to petition for 6.14/Costa-Hawkins increase but may seek determination; tenant may petition alleging unlawful increase; 60-day 6.14 notice benchmark; co-tenant vs subtenant distinction.
